phonics: u · ni · ver · si · ty → /juː/ + /nə/ + /vɜːr/ + /sə/ + /ti/
formula: uni- [全部] + vers [轉成一體] + -ity = 匯聚萬千學科的最高學府（大學）

family.example: Scientists are still exploring the mysteries of the universe.
Music is often called a universal language.

antonyms.example: She graduated from high school before entering university.

scene: 考上大學第一天，室友笑著說「在這裡有你沒事踢踢足球、念念書超自由」，結果教授突然出現把大家轉進期中考地獄。
example: She plans to study computer science at a top university.

phonics: pro · tect → /prə/ + /tekt/
formula: pro- [站在前面] + tect [遮蓋] = 擋在前面遮風避雨（保護）

family.example: Sunscreen offers great protection against UV rays.
Always wear protective glasses in the lab.

antonyms.example: The guards stood ready to protect the castle if enemies attack.
We must protect endangered animals instead of letting hunters harm them.

scene: 暴風雨來襲時，保鑣大喊一聲直接「撲來把鐵殼套」在你頭上，幫你擋掉所有飛來的樹枝和冰雹。
example: Parents always try their best to protect their children.

phonics: grab → /ɡræb/（單音節，短母音 /æ/ 嘴巴張大）
formula: grab [猛力抓住] = 一把抓過來（搶、順手拿）

family.example: He tried to grasp the rope before falling.
That catchy title is a real attention grabber.

antonyms.example: Release the handle slowly after you grab the brake.
Be careful not to drop the glass.

scene: 百貨週年慶大門一開，只見「哥拉布」一樣把架上的限量外套整把抓進懷裡，誰都搶不贏他。
example: Let's grab a quick coffee before the meeting starts.

phonics: con · sid · er → /kən/ + /sɪd/ + /ər/
formula: con- [一起] + sider [看星星占卜] = 慎重觀察評估（考慮、認為）

family.example: Thank you for taking my suggestion into consideration.
It was very considerate of you to bring me an umbrella.

antonyms.example: Don't ignore the warning signs when you consider the plan.

scene: 面對堆成山的髒碗盤，室友站在水槽前思考了十分鐘：「好啦，看在晚餐這麼好吃的份上，我是『肯洗的』！」
example: We need to consider all the options before making a decision.

phonics: al · low → /ə/ + /laʊ/
formula: al- [朝向] + low [點頭認可] = 點頭放行（允許）

family.example: Kids learn to save money from their weekly allowance.
Check the maximum allowable baggage weight before flying.

antonyms.example: The sign forbids visitors from taking flash photos.
Smoking is strictly prohibited inside the building.

scene: 夜市撈金魚老闆本來不給大人玩，結果看到「阿撈」一臉哀求，只好無奈點頭允許他下去撈兩隻。
example: Pets are not allowed inside this restaurant.

phonics: fault → /fɔːlt/（單音節，/ɔː/ 嘴唇微圓）
root: fault (失足、失敗，源自拉丁語 fallere)
formula: fault [失誤跌倒] = 出包的地方（過錯、缺點）

family.example: The fire was caused by faulty electrical wiring.
Her piano performance was completely faultless.

antonyms.example: We should judge the proposal on its own merits.

scene: 辦公室咖啡機突然噴泡沫，大家互指推卸責任，最後全場指向角落那個叫「佛特」的實習生：「絕對是你的錯！」
example: It wasn't your fault that the train got delayed.

phonics: dis · cuss → /dɪ/ + /skʌs/
formula: dis- [拆開] + cuss [敲擊] = 把問題敲開來四面拆解（討論）

family.example: We had a long discussion about the vacation budget.
The player suffered a mild concussion during the game.

antonyms.example: Let's not avoid the issue; we need to discuss it openly.

scene: 兩兄弟為了今晚要吃火鍋還是燒肉爭論不休，「弟死卡死」堅持不讓步，最後只好坐下來開家庭會議好好討論。
example: Let's meet tomorrow to discuss the project timeline.

phonics: up · set → /ʌp/ + /set/
formula: up- [向上翻] + set [擺好的東西] = 把平靜的心情或東西掀翻（難過、弄翻）

family.meaning: 令人心煩的、使人難過的
family.example: Hearing the bad news was deeply upsetting.
I really like your new desk setup.

antonyms.example: She stayed cheerful even when things didn't go as planned.
Try to stay calm instead of getting upset.

scene: 「阿婆塞」了一整鍋剛煮好的湯在桌邊，結果貓咪一跳直接整鍋翻倒，害阿婆當場心痛到超難過。
example: Don't get upset over a small mistake.

phonics: proud → /praʊd/（單音節，/aʊ/ 嘴巴由大張滑向嘟圓）
root: proud (勇敢的、有價值的，源自古法語 prud)
formula: proud [挺胸自豪] = 為成就感到光榮（驕傲的、自豪的）

family.example: She proudly showed everyone her gold medal.
He takes great pride in his cooking skills.

antonyms.example: You have nothing to be ashamed of; you should be proud.
Despite his success, he remains humble.

scene: 爺爺參加社區馬拉松，雖然「怕老得」跑不動，結果竟然衝線拿第一，站上頒獎台驕傲到下巴都要抬到天上去。
example: I am so proud of how hard you worked this year.

phonics: men · tion → /men/ + /ʃən/
formula: ment [心裡想] + -ion [動作] = 把心裡的想法帶出來講（提及）

family.example: Getting enough sleep is essential for mental health.
Several important details remained unmentioned in the report.

antonyms.example: Did he mention the cost, or did he omit that part?
She tried to conceal the truth from her friends.

scene: 聚會上大家聊得超嗨，只有「悶神」坐在角落都不說話，直到有人突然提到他的初戀，他才瞬間抬頭。
example: Did she mention when she will arrive?

phonics: rule → /ruːl/（單音節，長母音 /uː/ 嘴唇嘟圓）
root: rule (直尺、準則，源自拉丁語 regula)
formula: rule [畫線的直尺] = 大家必須照著走的基準（規則、統治）

family.example: Use a ruler to draw a straight line.
Regular exercise keeps your energy high.

antonyms.example: Without clear rules, the traffic would turn into chaos.
Every rule has an exception.

scene: 巷口那家滷味攤老闆訂了一個超嚴格的規定：「要買『滷喔』請排隊，插隊一律不賣！」
example: Breaking the safety rules in the factory is strictly forbidden.

phonics: in · cred · i · ble → /ɪn/ + /kred/ + /ə/ + /bəl/
meaning: 難以置信的、驚人的、極棒的
formula: in- [不] + cred [相信] + -ible [能] = 讓人無法相信的（難以置信的）

family.example: Make sure you get your news from credible sources.
She deserves all the credit for this incredible design.

antonyms.example: The movie plot wasn't very believable.
What looked like an ordinary day turned into an incredible adventure.

scene: 老闆清倉大拍賣全部打一折，旁邊店員驚呼：「老闆你這樣『硬虧得爆』，這價格簡直難以置信啊！」
example: The view from the top of the mountain was absolutely incredible.

phonics: br-ea-th → /br/ + /e/ + /θ/（ea 在此發短母音「ㄝ」，字尾 th 輕咬舌尖吐氣無聲）
root: bræth (古英語：呼出的熱氣/蒸氣)
formula: 古日耳曼語「熱氣/氣息」→ 呼出與吸入的空氣 → 氣息、一口氣

family.phonics: br-ea-the → ea 發長音「一」/iː/，字尾 e 不發音且讓 th 變有聲濁音 /ð/
family.example: Breathe deeply through your nose and relax your shoulders.

family.meaning: 氣喘吁吁的、上氣不接下氣的
family.example: She was breathless after running up five flights of stairs.

family.meaning: 壯觀的、令人屏息驚嘆的
family.example: The view from the top of the mountain was breathtaking.

antonyms.example: Keep plastic bags away from babies to prevent suffocation.
Sleep apnea causes brief pauses in breathing during sleep.

scene: 跑馬拉松快喘不過氣時，教練大喊：「深吸一口氣 (take a breath)，調整呼吸就『不累死』了！」
example: Take a deep breath and count to ten before you answer.

phonics: com · pli · ca · ted → /kɑm/ + /plə/ + /keɪ/ + /tɪd/（重音在第一音節，a 發長音 /eɪ/）
meaning: 複雜的、難懂糾葛的、繁瑣難解的
formula: com- [全部] + plic [折疊交疊了幾百層] + -ated = 像亂成一團的毛線球層層折疊打結 → 複雜難解的

family.example: Don't complicate the issue by adding unnecessary rules.

family.phonics: com · pli · ca · tion → 重音移到 -ca- /keɪ/，-tion 固定讀 /ʃən/
family.example: The surgery went smoothly without any complications.
Human memory is a remarkably complex system.

antonyms.example: The instructions are clear and simple to follow.

antonyms.meaning: 直截了當的、簡單明瞭的
antonyms.example: Installing the app is a straightforward process.

scene: 買了一台八百個零件的機械鐘，說明書密密麻麻像無字天書，複雜到你大喊：「這題我『扛不來，真想K他』！」
example: The tax laws in this country are far too complicated for ordinary citizens to understand.

phonics: ei · ther → /iː/（像一）或 /aɪ/（像愛）+ /ðɚ/（th 有聲咬舌音）
meaning: （兩者中）任一個、兩方都；（否定句中）也不；either...or... (不是...就是...)
formula: ā- [任何] + hwæther [兩者中挑一個] = 在兩者岔路中取任一端，或否定時兩者皆非

family.phonics: nei · ther → n + either（兩者皆非）
family.example: Neither of the two restaurants was open on Monday.

family.phonics: wh-e-ther → wh 發 /w/（h 不發音），e 發短音「ㄝ」
family.example: I don't know whether he will join us tonight.

antonyms.example: Neither answer is correct.
You can take both books home today.

scene: 報紙上左邊一篇八卦、右邊一篇頭條，編輯說：「兩者任選『一則 (either)』刊登就好，我全都要的話讀者會看花眼！」
example: You can choose either option; both of them have great advantages.

phonics: ex · pense → /ɪk/ + /spens/（重音在第二音節，字尾 e 不發音）
formula: ex- [向外掏出] + pens [秤量付錢] = 口袋裡的銀兩不斷往外支付支出 → 開銷/費用

family.example: Eating out every night can get very expensive.
The company cut its advertising expenditure by 20 percent.
How much did you spend on that jacket?

antonyms.example: His monthly income easily covers his living expenses.
We used our savings to buy our first home.

scene: 去高檔餐廳結帳看到天價帳單，荷包裡的鈔票像水龍頭爆開一樣「一克死貴、一口氣噴死 (expense)」，開銷太大了！
example: We need to cut down our monthly living expenses by cooking at home.

phonics: w-eir-d → /w/ + /ɪr/（同 ear）+ /d/（單音節，別唸成兩個音節）
root: wyrd (命運/不可預料的神力命運女神)
formula: 像神秘命運女神一樣超乎常理、不可捉摸的超自然現象 → 離奇奇怪的

family.example: People called him a weirdo because he talked to his plants.
The room was weirdly quiet when we walked in.

antonyms.example: It is completely normal to feel nervous before a speech.
Just an ordinary Tuesday morning at the office.

scene: 隔壁鄰居「威爾的 (weird)」行為超古怪，半夜三點穿著青蛙裝在陽台用吸塵器吸空氣！
example: I had a really weird dream where cats could fly airplanes.

phonics: a · pol · o · gize → /ə/ + /pɑ/ + /lə/ + /dʒaɪz/（g 在 i 前發 /dʒ/，字尾 -ize 讀 /aɪz/）
formula: apo- [撇清前嫌] + logos [用言語認錯化解] + -ize = 用真誠言語承認過失以修復關係 → 道歉

family.example: She wrote a sincere letter of apology to her friend.

family.phonics: a · pol · o · get · ic → 重音移到 -get- /dʒet/
family.example: He gave me an apologetic smile after spilling the coffee.

antonyms.example: Don't blame others for your own mistakes.
He tried to defend his rude behavior instead of saying sorry.

scene: 「阿婆老這愛死」面子，以前從不低頭，今天踩到人竟然90度鞠躬狂道歉認錯！
example: He sincerely apologized for arriving late to the interview.

phonics: ri · dic · u · lous → /rɪ/ + /dɪk/ + /jə/ + /ləs/（重音在第二音節 dic）
formula: ridere [惹人發笑] + -culous = 荒唐愚蠢到讓人失笑的 → 荒謬可笑的

family.example: It is cruel to ridicule someone for their accent.

family.phonics: ri · dic · u · lous · ly → 字尾加 -ly
family.example: The tickets for that concert were ridiculously expensive.

antonyms.example: That sounds like a very reasonable price.
Wearing a coat in winter is a sensible choice.

scene: 四十度大夏天穿羽絨大衣去海灘衝浪，荒謬可笑到旁人笑翻，「你弟哭了死」也還是覺得超荒唐！
example: Spending a thousand dollars on a pair of plastic slippers is totally ridiculous.

phonics: a · dor · a · ble → /ə/ + /dɔːr/ + /ə/ + /bəl/（重音在 dor）
formula: ad- [朝向] + ore [敬愛讚美] + -able = 討喜到讓人忍不住由衷呵護喜愛的 → 極可愛的

family.phonics: a · dore → /ə/ + /dɔːr/（字尾 e 不發音）
family.example: I absolutely adore small kittens.

family.phonics: a · dor · a · bly → 去 e 加 y
family.example: The baby smiled adorably at the camera.

antonyms.example: That monster in the movie looked hideous.
The smell from the garbage was repulsive.

scene: 小柴犬「阿朵」圓滾滾又會歪頭笑，超級「惹人抱 (adorable)」，可愛到把大家心都融化了！
example: The golden retriever puppy is so adorable that everyone wants to cuddle it.

phonics: fig · ured → /fɪɡ/ + /jɚd/（u 在此發 /jɚ/，ed 讀濁音 /d/）
meaning: 想到了、早就料到/猜到了 (I figured)、弄清楚了 (figured out)
formula: figure [腦海勾勒輪廓] + -ed [已琢磨定案] = 腦袋早已琢磨明白 → 早就猜到了/料想到了

family.example: Let's figure out how to solve this puzzle together.

family.phonics: dis + figured → 破壞外貌形狀
family.example: The old statue was disfigured by years of acid rain.

antonyms.example: I completely overlooked that important detail.
I misjudged the distance and missed the target.

scene: 一進客廳看到滿桌空披薩盒，你嘆口氣：「我就猜到了 (I figured)！這擺明是『飛哥的』傑作！」
example: I figured you would be hungry after the long flight, so I ordered pizza.

phonics: ex · plain → /ɪk/ + /spleɪn/（ai 合起來發長音 /eɪ/）
formula: ex- [徹底] + planus [鋪平展現] = 把糾結複雜的道理整個攤平鋪開講 → 解釋說明

family.phonics: ex · pla · na · tion → 注意拼字沒有 i！重音在 na
family.example: He gave a clear explanation of the new policy.

family.phonics: ex · plan · a · to · ry → 重音在 plan
family.example: Please read the explanatory notes at the bottom of the page.

antonyms.example: Your complicated chart will only confuse the audience.
Technical jargon can obscure the main point.

scene: 客服人員超有耐心，把複雜條款解釋到「一個死不累 (explain)」的地步，講了三小時還是面帶微笑！
example: Could you please explain how this software algorithm works?

phonics: as · sume → /ə/ + /suːm/（u 在此發「屋」/uː/，字尾 e 不發音）
formula: as- [在未驗證前] + sumere [擅自先拿來當真] = 先入為主認定 → 假定/設想

family.phonics: as · sump · tion → u 變短音 /ʌ/，中間多了 p
family.example: We shouldn't make decisions based on false assumptions.
The spy traveled under an assumed name.

antonyms.example: You need evidence to prove your theory.
Always verify the facts before sharing news.

scene: 愛八卦的「阿叔母 (assume)」沒查證就擅自假定鄰居一定中樂透了，結果只是買了一台二手車！
example: Never assume anything without checking the facts first.

phonics: n-er-ve → /n/ + /ɝː/（捲舌母音 er）+ /v/（字尾 e 不發音）
formula: 大腦中傳遞感知與勇氣力量的纖維軸索 → 神經/膽識

family.example: I always get nervous right before a job interview.
That was a pretty nervy move on the racetrack.

antonyms.example: He showed cowardice by running away from responsibility.
Her timidity kept her from raising her hand.

scene: 大家站在透明玻璃橋上腿都軟了，「那婦 (nerve)」竟然膽量超群、神經大條，在橋上跳繩！
example: It takes a lot of nerve to speak in front of hundreds of people.

phonics: pre · tend → /prɪ/ + /tend/（重音在第二音節 tend）
formula: pre- [在別人眼前] + tend [拉起假幕布掩飾真相] = 在人前做假動作 → 假裝

family.example: She dropped all pretense of being polite and walked out.

family.meaning: 做作浮誇的、自命不凡的
family.example: The restaurant was too pretentious for my taste.

antonyms.example: He decided to reveal his true feelings.
She admitted that she didn't know the answer.

scene: 碰瓷大叔在腳踏車前面誇張「撲地喊好疼的 (pretend)」，結果假裝被監視器拍得一清二楚！
example: He pretended not to hear the alarm clock and pulled the blanket over his head.

phonics: ap · pre · ci · ate → /ə/ + /priː/ + /ʃi/ + /eɪt/（ci 發「希」/ʃi/，ate 發 /eɪt/）
formula: ap- [看到對方的價值] + pretium [賦予崇高身價] + -ate = 重視認同對方的付出 → 感激/欣賞

family.phonics: ap · pre · ci · a · tion → 重音在 a /eɪ/
family.example: Please accept this gift as a token of our appreciation.

family.phonics: ap · pre · ci · a · tive → -tive 讀輕音 /t̬ɪv/
family.example: The audience was very appreciative of the pianist's performance.

antonyms.example: A new car begins to depreciate as soon as you drive it off the lot.
I despise people who are cruel to animals.

scene: 年輕人幫阿伯扛米上五樓，「阿伯瑞（非常）謝他 (appreciate)」，感動到眼眶泛淚！
example: I truly appreciate all your help during this difficult transition.

phonics: ex · act · ly → /ɪɡ/ + /zækt/ + /li/（ex 在母音前濁化成 /ɪɡz/）
meaning: 確切地、正是如此、一點也沒錯
formula: ex- [徹底精準] + act [做到分毫不差] + -ly = 絲毫不差 → 正是如此！

family.example: Can you tell me the exact time the train leaves?

family.phonics: ex · act · ness → 加 -ness 變名詞
family.example: Watchmaking requires extreme exactness.

antonyms.example: The flight takes approximately three hours.
I vaguely remember meeting him years ago.

scene: 射飛鏢「一個扎在克（刻）度裡 (exactly)」，分毫不差命中紅心，裁判大喊：「正是如此！」
example: That is exactly what I was trying to tell you all along.

phonics: w-a-s-te → a_e 規則發長音 /eɪ/，字尾 e 不發音
formula: 把好好的一整片資源變成無用的荒地廢墟 → 浪費

family.example: Leaving the lights on all day is very wasteful.
Years of drought turned the farm into a wasteland.

antonyms.example: We must conserve water during the dry season.
Cherish every moment you spend with your family.

scene: 點了一整桌滿漢全席吃不完，硬要拿去「餵死他 (waste)」家的寵物豬，太浪費了！
example: Do not waste your precious time arguing with internet trolls.

phonics: t-ou-gh → ou 在此發短音 /ʌ/，字尾 gh 發「夫」/f/
meaning: 堅韌頑強的、棘手艱難的
formula: 材料緊密拉不斷嚼不爛 → 堅韌頑強的/難啃的硬骨頭

family.example: Mental toughness is key to winning a marathon.

family.phonics: tough · en → 加 -en 變動詞「使變強硬」
family.example: The government plans to toughen safety regulations.

antonyms.example: Be careful with that box; the glass inside is fragile.
This steak is super tender and juicy.

scene: 對手看這硬漢怎麼打都打不倒，韌性強到不行，最後舉白旗說：「這場硬仗我真『他服 (tough)』了！」
example: She had a tough childhood but grew up into a remarkably resilient person.

phonics: f-ear → /f/ + /ɪr/（ear 唸起來同耳 ear）
formula: 突如其來的危險襲來時內心的震顫反應 → 恐懼

family.example: Residents were fearful of another earthquake.
The fearless firefighter rushed into the burning building.

antonyms.example: It took great courage to speak the truth.
Practice gives you confidence on stage.

scene: 「飛兒 (fear)」半夜走進黑漆漆的鬼屋，被突然彈出來的骷髏嚇得魂魄飛上天！
example: He conquered his deep fear of flying and boarded the plane.

phonics: ex · pect → /ɪk/ + /spekt/（重音在第二音節 pect）
formula: ex- [伸頭往外] + spect [凝視觀望] = 伸長脖子朝門外看人來了沒 → 期待/預期

family.phonics: ex · pec · ta · tion → 重音在 ta /teɪ/
family.example: The movie far exceeded our expectations.

family.phonics: un + ex · pec · ted → un- 表否定「出乎意料」
family.meaning: 出乎意料的、突如其來的
family.example: We received an unexpected visit from our cousin.

antonyms.example: I doubt it will rain today; the sky is clear.
Never despair even when things look difficult.

scene: 訂的炸雞外送遲到一小時，餓到前胸貼後背，「一刻不停死盼他 (expect)」按門鈴！
example: We expect the delivery to arrive before noon.

phonics: gor · geous → /ɡɔːr/ + /dʒəs/（geous 固定讀輕音 /dʒəs/）
meaning: 極其美麗動人的、華麗華美的
formula: 脖子掛滿璀璨華美珠寶項鍊的美人 → 極其美麗動人的

family.example: The ballroom was gorgeously decorated with roses.

antonyms.example: That abandoned building is really ugly.
She prefers plain clothes over flashy outfits.

scene: 新娘穿著流金晚禮服走進會場，全場賓客屏息：「天啊，真的『夠正死 (gorgeous)』了！」
example: The bride looked breathtakingly gorgeous in her silk wedding dress.

phonics: awe · some → /ɔː/（aw 發長音「喔」）+ /səm/（e 不發音）
formula: awe [讓人屏息驚呆] + -some = 棒到讓人肅然起敬 → 太棒了！

family.example: We watched the northern lights in complete awe.

family.phonics: aw · ful → /ɔː/ + /fəl/（注意：意義反轉成極糟糕）
family.example: The weather was awful all weekend.

antonyms.example: That coffee tasted awful.
I had a terrible headache last night.

scene: 街頭藝人單手倒立同時轉三個呼拉圈，路人看呆集體尖叫：「喔～神 (awesome) 啊，太棒了！」
example: You passed the exam with full marks? That is absolutely awesome!

phonics: daugh · ter → /dɔː/（augh 在此發「喔」/ɔː/，gh 不發音）+ /tər/
formula: 古印歐語中負責照料家庭的親生女孩 → 女兒

family.example: She bought a birthday gift for her goddaughter.

family.phonics: daughter + in + law → 法律上的女兒
family.example: Her daughter-in-law is a talented architect.

antonyms.example: Their son just started elementary school.

scene: 爸爸是個超級女兒奴，為了寵寶貝「女兒 (daughter)」，甘願「倒貼」所有私房錢買公主裙！
example: Their youngest daughter just graduated from medical school.

phonics: con · grat · u · la · tions → /kən/ + /ɡrætʃ/ + /ə/ + /leɪ/ + /ʃənz/（tu 連讀成 /tʃə/，重音在 la）
root: grat / gratus (喜悅、感激、討人喜歡)
formula: con- [大家一起] + grat [分享喜悅與恩典] + -ations = 大家聚在一起分享喜慶祝福 → 恭喜！祝賀！

family.phonics: con · grat · u · late → 重音在 grat
family.example: Let me congratulate you on your promotion!
I am very grateful for your kindness.
She expressed her deep gratitude to the doctors.

antonyms.example: We offered our sincere condolences to his family.
He received harsh criticism instead of praise.

scene: 全村只有他「肯抓就」舉起「雷神」索爾的鎚子，大家衝上來拉炮大喊：恭喜恭喜 (congratulations)！
example: Congratulations on landing your dream job after all the hard work!

phonics: sud · den · ly → /sʌd/ + /ən/ + /li/（u 發短音「啊」/ʌ/，重音在第一音節）
formula: sub- [暗中] + ire [走來] + -ly = 毫無預兆暗中冒出來 → 突然

family.example: A sudden storm forced us to cancel the picnic.

family.phonics: sud · den · ness → 加 -ness 變名詞
family.example: The suddenness of the announcement shocked everyone.

antonyms.example: The sky gradually turned dark after sunset.
The train slowly pulled into the station.

scene: 你走在暗巷裡，轉角處「突然」跳出一群朋友「撒花等你 (suddenly)」給你驚喜派對！
example: Suddenly, the lights went out and the entire room was pitch-black.
